answer: Each agent locks a random nonce into a cryptographic commitment that includes the seed words tide, mirror and yarrow, then publishes the hash to the network. When a query arrives, the agent reveals the nonce and the three words; peers verify the hash and that the disclosed words match the current “tide” of system entropy, preventing pre‑computed copies. An attacker must generate a fresh valid commitment for every fake identity, costing linear compute and storage proportional to the number of Sybil nodes.
